constraintConflict: Producing 2-4 new contracts would require reopening a closed source class, substituting the immutable Emberglass contract, or introducing an unavailable external topology.
futilityReasons: The relevant combat, reward, run-state and policy source files are unchanged from the source basis of the accepted structural closures.
Existing combat-state/operator, trace/history, arithmetic residue, local identity/transform and reward/acquisition paths are closed.
Option 2 authorised exactly one persistent contract; Emberglass was that selected tuple and is immutable INCONCLUSIVE_AT_CAP, with repair, rerun and substitution prohibited.
No source-and-evidence-selected external semantic producer/consumer/payoff tuple remains. Constructing one would be speculative.

rejectedSourceClasses.reason: Any new coupling over current statuses, healing, Ward, Ember, Facet or damage is an existing-state/operator or previously screened structural family; Weak-mend was the sole eligible residual and failed closed.
Changing order, a transient marker, card-zone handling, target identity or same-fight lifecycle maps to immutable relation/history or identity-transform closures.
An additive relic routed through ordinary pools or rewards is the closed native acquisition/reward class; post-Shatter reward feedback was expressly rejected as its alias.

The only Option 2 tuple was Emberglass Memory. Its source-identity process completed no probe output and is immutable inconclusive non-decision evidence; a different carrier would be a prohibited substitution.

A wholly new primitive has no accepted evidence-selected producer, consumer, bounded payoff or activation objective. Selecting one from source alone would guess rather than produce a non-alias contract.

filterOrder: reject the selected Emberglass tuple and every substitute
deterministicRankingRule.survivorOrder: ascending changed source files, then new mutable state fields, then new event types, then gameplay RNG calls, then lexical contract ID
